title: Sharp primitive-integral residue obstructions for genus-zero strata with multiple zeros and only simple poles
difficulty_reason: H2: old2063 settles only one zero with cutoff s-2. Splitting that zero covers the large total-weight range but cannot realize the new intermediate range max(a_i)<T<=s-2. The author uses a stable genus-zero decomposition with one zero per component, constructs two-component signed-residue configurations with controlled nodal residues and primitive gcd, then inducts on the zero count. The converse uses a minimal counterexample and a leaf component to enforce the sharp maximum-zero-order cutoff. This new stable gluing/induction is the distinct burden; the sufficient old H2 connection-tree judgment is reused without another qualification.

editorial_notes: Retain original author statements/proofs and all inline TikZ illustrations unchanged; author mathematics is not independently certified, corrected or supplemented.
Types have strictly positive zero orders, higher pole orders b_j>=2 and s simple poles. Preserve the partition sum 2g-2 and the exclusion of the empty one-simple-pole strata.
Residual space is C^p times (C*)^s with total sum zero: residues at higher order poles may vanish, simple-pole residues cannot.
Author residue convention is 2*pi*i times the usual analytic residue; retain it for gluing, flat periods and cylinder statements.
Primitive integral signed residue data use the collective gcd of all positive integers equal to1 and a common nonzero complex scaling factor, not pairwise coprimality.
